own_solution.law: Snell's law n1 sin(theta1) = n2 sin(theta2); theta2 = arcsin(1.0*sin40/1.5)
assumptions: Camera has no physical influence on the ray

defect_reasons.other: With T4914 (and to a lesser degree T6894) the text does not say explicitly whether the stated 40 degree angle of incidence is the angle before or after the 11 degree tilt; the intended reading (tilt from 40 to 51 degrees) gives the certified 31.2047 degrees, but a reader could take 40 degrees as the angle at observation.

notes: Checked certified answers independently: base arcsin(sin40/1.5)=arcsin(0.428525)=25.374; q=6: arcsin(sin46/1.5)=arcsin(0.479560)=28.657; q=11: arcsin(sin51/1.5)=arcsin(0.518097)=31.205; q=14: arcsin(sin54/1.5)=arcsin(0.539345)=32.639. All match; all transmitted angles are well below any total-internal-reflection concern (light goes into the denser medium). D claims hold: the camera and an earlier, finished experiment have no causal path to the refraction angle. T85A3/T4914 are a true minimal pair (same 11 degrees, same laser and plane-of-incidence wording, differing only in 'in an earlier experiment' vs 'before the refraction was observed'). T0BCD/T6894 are correctly not claimed as a minimal pair. TB680 and TE753 are declared numeral-free twins of T0BCD and T85A3, which resolves my provisional pass-1 rendering_not_minimal flag; I withdraw it here. Scene clause (camera on tripod) is consistent with the base problem.
